speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, does it look like bile (green) or food?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby seems to be in significant pain with abdominal tenderness and reduced feeding. Has he passed any stool or gas recently, and if so, was it green or tarry black? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray; REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal X-ray suggests an obstruction with no gas in the rectum. Has the baby passed any stool recently, and if so, was it "currant jelly" in appearance?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of fever and the normal urinalysis help rule out infectious causes or metabolic issues. Given the X-ray findings of dilated bowel with no distal gas and the severe tenderness, have you noticed any "currant jelly" stools or signs of an inguinal hernia? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound is normal, which makes midgut volvulus or intussusception less likely. The combination of an X-ray showing obstruction and no gas in the rectum strongly suggests a distal blockage. Did the baby ever pass meconium within the first 48 hours after birth?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease.

The combination of delayed or difficult meconium passage, abdominal distension, bilious vomiting, and failure to thrive is highly characteristic of Hirschsprung disease. I am requesting an Anorectal Manometry and/or Rectal Biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy
